ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The input-output transfer function of a plant is \( H(s) = \frac{100}{s(s+10)^2} \). The plant is placed in a unity negative feedback configuration as shown in the figure. The gain margin of the system under closed-loop unity negative feedback is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a standard single-input single-output unity negative feedback control block diagram. The input r on the left enters the summing node Σ, the reference input terminal is marked with a positive sign, and the feedback input terminal is marked with a negative sign; the summing output u enters a plant block. The block is labeled H(s)=100/[s(s+10)^2], the output on the right is y, and y returns to the negative terminal of the summing node through a direct feedback line, with no additional controller or sensor dynamics seen. Therefore the open-loop loop transfer function is taken as L(s)=H(s). Reasoning calculation: L(s)=100/[s(s+10)^2]. Let s=jω, then L(jω)=100/[jω(10+jω)^2]. Its phase is ∠L(jω)=-90°-2 tan^{-1}(ω/10). The phase crossover frequency satisfies ∠L(jω_pc)=-180°, so -90°-2 tan^{-1}(ω_pc/10)=-180°, giving tan^{-1}(ω_pc/10)=45°, therefore ω_pc=10 rad/s. At this frequency, |L(j10)|=100/(|j10| |10+j10|^2)=100/(10 × (10^2+10^2))=100/(10 × 200)=0.05. The gain margin GM=1/0.05=20. Expressed in dB, it is 20 log10(20)=26.02 dB, approximately 26 dB.
